A pair of world title matches, plus the annual ladder matches take place on Saturday night

        Every year, Money in the Bank sets up months of WWE programming. One man and one woman will earn an automatic shot at any title of their choosing to be used at any moment.The drama and suspense of not knowing when and where the cash-in will happen makes for compelling television, and the ladder matches to determine who has the honor of being Money in the Bank briefcase holder will go down on Saturday in New Orleans.In addition to the two ladder matches, two titles will be on the line, with Roman Reigns defending the world heavyweight championship against old foe LA Knight, and Stephanie Vaquer putting the women's world championship on the line in a triple threat match against Becky Lynch and Liv Morgan. In addition, Oba Femi is set to clash with Bronson Reed in a match between physical powerhouses.With so much action set for Saturday, the CBS Sports wrestling experts sat down to make their picks for who will emerge victorious at Money in the Bank.
World Heavyweight Championship -- Roman Reigns (c) vs. LA Knight: While I appreciate that the Knight character is one of the only people in WWE who remembers that Reigns' incredible title run was almost entirely the product of endless cheating, he's not ending Reigns' current run as champion. There's a better chance if Reigns loses the belt on Saturday, it's a product of the Money in the Bank winner cashing in than Knight winning the belt. Pick: Roman Reigns retains the title -- Brent Brookhouse (also Shakiel Mahjouri)Bron Breakker vs. Je'Von Evans vs. Trick Williams vs. Penta vs. CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens (Men's Money in the Bank ladder match): WWE have assembled a compelling cast for this year's ladder match. Every man, with the exception of Evans, has a reasonable case for winning the match. Breakker and Williams could launch into the main event scene, Punk has history with the briefcase, plus he and Owens would elevate its status. But after Raw in Mexico City, Penta is my pick. Penta put on a classic against world heavyweight champion Reigns. It helped people visualize Penta as a world champion. Winning Money in the Bank is the easiest way to complete the luchador's bridge between upper midcard and main event. Pick: Penta wins -- MahjouriAs mentioned by Shakiel, you can make a valid case for five different winners here, though I'd personally eliminate Williams from consideration. I think this comes down to Punk or Owens as the winner since Reigns isn't around enough for Penta or Breakker to be compelling holders, and Breakker is likely tied up with Oba Femi for the foreseeable future anyway. I'll say Owens, simply because I think he would be a fun guy to see strategizing how and when to cash in. Pick: Kevin Owens wins -- Brookhouse
Sol Ruca vs. Lola Vice vs. Jacy Jayne vs. Roxanne Perez vs. Lash Legend vs. Tiffany Stratton (Women's Money in the Bank ladder match): The women's ladder match really emphasizes how the briefcase can turn a midcarder into a world champion. Excluding Stratton, no woman in the match has won a world title. Legend and Stratton are solid frontrunners, but Perez has a more compelling story to explore. Putting the briefcase on her creates conflict with her Judgment Day teammate Liv Morgan. The stable has been an important part of Raw for a very long time, and this gives them another storyline to dig into. Pick: Roxanne Perez wins -- Mahjouri (also Brookhouse)Oba Femi vs. Bronson Reed: You can't have Femi retire Brock Lesnar and subsequently lose to Reed. It's that simple. Femi must look indestructible until he eventually crosses paths with Reigns, potentially at WrestleMania next year. That's a long time for now, but the payoff works best if Femi remains an unstoppable force. Pick: Oba Femi wins -- Mahjouri (also Brookhouse)Women's World Championship -- Stephanie Vaquer (c) vs. Becky Lynch vs. Liv Morgan: Vaquer recently regained the belt and WWE doesn't flip titles around quickly very often. The triple threat nature of the match sets up Morgan to be able to cheat in various ways, but I could see Perez's involvement muddying things up if she won Money in the Bank earlier in the night. This is set up for Vaquer to get a win and retain the title in a way that doesn't feel satisfying for Lynch or Morgan as both continue to chase the champion. Pick: Stephanie Vaquer retains the title -- Brookhouse (also Mahjouri)

        Mississippi Valley State University men's basketball player Qingfang Pang has been detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Pang, who transferred to Mississippi Valley State from Monroe University in New York this offseason, is in ICE custody at the Richwood Correctional Center in Richwood, Louisana, according to the ICE database.WJTV, which first reported the news on Wednesday night, said that Pang was detained on Sept. 29 for overstaying his visa. Pang's attorney, Marcus Session, told WJTV that his client was on his way to New York to be with his sponsor — who is a family friend — to get his visa issue sorted out before being detained by ICE."He wants to resume going to school," Session told WJTV. "He wants to play college basketball. He wants to be a 21-year-old kid who's just trying to make a life for himself."
        
            
                Inside the most absurd nonconference schedule: Why Mississippi Valley State has no home games for two months
                
                    Isaac Trotter                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Pang played high school basketball at St. Benedict's Preparatory School in New Jersey and Christ the King High School in New York before enrolling at Monroe. During the 2025-26 season with Monroe, Pang appeared in 31 games and averaged 8.3 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game.
Mississippi Valley State University, which is playing one of the most unconventional schedules of any Division I college basketball program this season, opens the 2026-27 campaign on the road against Oklahoma on Nov. 6. The Delta Devils also face Washington, Oregon, Arkansas, Michigan, UConn, Mississippi State, Ohio State and Texas Tech in nonconference play.

        The Vanderbilt Commodores will have their young phenom at quarterback when they host No. 9 Ole Miss on Saturday afternoon. After missing last week's game against Georgia with an injury, five-star freshman Jared Curtis is expected to return against the Rebels, sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.Curtis last played in Week 4 when the Commodores lost to Auburn on the road. Curtis took a beating in that game as he ran the ball 18 times, including four sacks. As a result, Curtis was sidelined when Vanderbilt traveled to Georgia last weekend.Veteran Blaze Berlowitz got the start in that matchup, and he completed 52.2% of his passes for 190 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Berlowitz initially won the starting job out of camp until Curtis surpassed him on the depth chart and made his first start against NC State in Week 3.Through four games, Curtis has shown flashes of why he was a five-star recruit and the No. 2 overall player in the 2026 signing class, per 247Sports. Curtis has connected on 64.3% of his throws for 746 yards, four touchdowns and three interceptions. Decision-making has been a problem early, but that's to be expected from a young quarterback.
The return of Curtis elevates the ceiling of the Vanderbilt offense, one that has a chance to score some points on Ole Miss this weekend. The Rebels' defense has left a lot to be desired, especially against the run. That unit ranks 127th nationally with 194.8 rushing yards allowed per game.That means the 'Dores should be able to lean on running back Sedrick Alexander, who leads the team with 200 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns. If Alexander can keep the chains moving for Vanderbilt, it will take some pressure off Curtis, who will be making the second start of his college career.
Curtis, a Nashville native, has the opportunity to cement himself as a hometown hero if Vanderbilt can pull off the upset of Ole Miss. The Commodores haven't beaten the Rebels since 2018.

title: Meet Santiago Castaneda, Colombian-American shining in Germany and potential USMNT gem - CBS Sports
description: The Tampa native has represented the U.S. at the youth level but is also eligible to represent Colombia
body:
The Tampa native has represented the U.S. at the youth level but is also eligible to represent Colombia

    2:42 pm ET

            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The path of American soccer players has shifted over the years as there are now more Americans performing at high levels in Europe than ever before, but much of that is due to being able to build on the success of those who came before them. Few know that better than Santiago Castaneda, who has now made it from Tampa, Florida, to the Bundesliga with Paderborn, scoring his first goal this season and leading the club to their first Bundesliga victory in 2,431 days. It has been a long road for the club since being relegated in the 2019-20 season before Castaneda helped them get back to the top flight, and the club journey mirrors that of the Colombian-American midfielder.Soccer is something that is in Castaneda's blood. His father, Carlos, played professionally in Colombia, and his brother also played, so at a young age, Castaneda was exposed to soccer and what it meant to be a professional, which was important when making the decision not to go to Michigan for college and instead take a trial with MSV Duisburg in the third division of Germany, which was one of many situations where Castaneda bet on himself and it worked out."We took this decision together to go to the third division in Germany, and we all had this passion for the game where we knew that professional soccer was the next step for me ... One main thing that my father, my family, taught me when I was younger is respect and discipline, and this is what you need to go far in life, but not only as a player, but as a person," Castaneda told CBS Sports. "So I think with that I was able to take that and work for my dreams and work hard for what I wanted, and I think without my family, none of this could have happened for sure."Coming from the Tampa Bay Rowdies system, on paper, the jump to the German third division may have been one that was at a similar level to the United Soccer League, but due to the presence of promotion and relegation, the room for upward mobility is high. It's also easier to believe in yourself when there's not only a support system, but when you've also seen more Americans performing at high levels, be it Champions League soccer or regulars in the European game. When Castaneda was getting started with the Rowdies, Christian Pulisic became the first American to play in a Champions League final when he lifted the trophy with Chelsea, conquering a new frontier for American soccer players.
Now you also have an entire generation that doesn't know life without America having a top-flight domestic league, and the fruits of that show among the young talent abroad that Castaneda is part of."Before, you didn't see so much, and now you're seeing so much more happening, and of course that says a lot about the American system and the way they're handling things and the way they're producing players, and it seems like we're going in a good direction, and yeah, I think for me it's really special coming from the Tampa area," Castaneda said. "There aren't that many products that come from there so it's a little bit more special for me to represent that area. I think overall American soccer association, they're doing everything the right way, and it could get better and better as time goes by."Even with an international break coming to a close, where Mauricio Pochettino has called in younger prospects from all over, Castaneda wasn't part of the USMNT squad despite having caps with the youth sides where he played alongside Diego Kochen and Brooklyn Raines. In the past, it would've been unheard of for a Bundesliga starter to miss a camp, and while he's focused on getting called into the USMNT, there haven't been conversations with Mauricio Pochettino. Also eligible to represent Colombia, Castaneda is open to either country as he has heritage with both.
European goalsHe's already accomplished one goal of making it to Europe, and now that he's in the Bundesliga, the next goal of representing a national team likely won't be far behind. At 21, Castaneda has already made 73 appearances for Paderborn, gaining plenty of experience along the way as a defensive midfielder and a box-to-box midfielder, and when he looks back at where he came from in Tampa, it's astounding."If you look back at three or four years ago, I was still playing high school soccer, which is really crazy to think about, and every time I think about that, it gives me less pressure on myself. It's like I can be really proud of how far I've gotten, but it's not a thing to slow me down and get relaxed; it's to keep me pushing and be a role model for the people in Tampa and the United States," Castaneda said.Getting to this point in a fast rise of only five years from Tampa to the Bundesliga has been a journey for Castaneda, but it's one that's far from over. He said that seeing his peers get the call to the USMNT makes him want to push more to get to that stage himself, and continuing on this current path, opportunities will come. 
There hasn't been a better time when it comes to depth among American soccer players, which does make it tougher to get national team opportunities, but it also makes them that much more gratifying when they happen. Of course, if he continues on this path, there's the potential for dual national panic between the United States and Colombia, but for Castaneda and Paderborn, that'd be quite a good problem to have.

        No. 2 Georgia is traveling to No. 6 Alabama on Saturday night for a rematch of the 2025 SEC Championship Game that will serve as a midseason gauge for where two of the nation's undefeated blue bloods stand. While the stakes of these regular-season showdowns are less seismic in the 12-team College Football Playoff era, they are still high.The winner will be on an inside track to lock up a CFP spot and a possible return trip to the SEC title game. The loser will be operating on a minimal margin for error with plenty of SEC treachery still ahead. While UGA enters as the higher-ranked team, Alabama has proven more.Coming off a 56-23 win at Mississippi State, the Crimson Tide have scored between 45 and 56 points in every game while knocking off four Power Four opponents in a run that also includes against a road win over a solid Kentucky team.Georgia is off to a 3-0 start in SEC play, but those three victories came against the conference's three worst offenses. This will be the toughest test yet for the Bulldogs, by a wide margin, as they seek their first road win over Alabama since 2007.
As we get set for a battle between the nation's two highest-scoring offenses, let's break down who has the edge at each position. Quarterback Alabama sophomore star Keelon Russell is No. 2 in this week's QBPR, which is three spots ahead of No. 5 Gunner Stockton. But Stockton gets the nod in a great quarterback battle because of the experience factor. He's started in SEC Championship and College Football Playoff games. He was nails down the stretch inside a hostile environment at Tennessee last season and also led Georgia to regular-season wins against teams like Ole Miss and Texas. Additionally, if Hurricane Isaias dumps heavy rainfall on Bryant-Denny Stadium, it will favor Stockton. He is tied for 106th nationally in air yards per attempt at 7.9 compared to 10.1 air yards per attempt for Russell.
Russell passed his first big test as Alabama's starter last week with flying colors in a win at Mississippi State. But this is a new level of challenge as he leads the Crimson Tide against a Georgia team ranked No. 7 nationally in total defense. Edge: GeorgiaSkill talent Don't look now, but Alabama junior star Ryan Coleman-Williams hasn't been officially credited with a drop since Week 1. Additionally, sophomore Lotzeir Brooks is in the midst of what appears to be a breakout season for the Crimson Tide, and Rico Scott has emerged as a reliable option with three touchdown grabs.Georgia has some big-play potential in its receiver room, but it's an inexperienced unit that still has something to prove. No one has seized the mantle and emerged as a clear game-changer. UGA offensive coordinator Mike Bobo deploys his deep tight end group creatively, but there's no Brock Bowers in that room. 
Both teams boast similarly deep running back groups, but Coleman-Williams and Brooks give the Crimson Tide a playmaking edge in the skill position realm. Edge: AlabamaOffensive line Georgia is tied for first in the SEC with eight rushes of 25-plus yards, which has propelled the Bulldogs to No. 3 nationally in yards per rush at 6.49. Alabama's offensive line appears improved, and that's reflected in a respectable 4.85 yards per carry. But the Crimson Tide haven't been as explosive.In the passing game, both teams have faced blitzes on roughly 37.5% of their dropbacks. Alabama has allowed pressure on 33.9% of its dropbacks compared to just 26.6% for Georgia. UGA's 3.5% sack rate reflects the quick-hit nature of UGA's passing attack, but it's substantially better than Alabama's 8.1% mark. Edge: Georgia
Front seven Alabama's scoring defense ranks 51st, compared to Georgia's 12th. But that's largely a reflection of the fact that the Bulldogs have played the SEC's three least-potent offensive teams (Arkansas, Oklahoma and Vanderbilt). The Crimson Tide have faced five top-60 offenses, including a pair of top-15 units in Mississippi State and South Carolina.Playing better competition, Alabama's front seven has been more disruptive, amassing 16 sacks compared to Georgia's 13. Against Mississippi State's vaunted offense last week, the Crimson Tide totaled nine tackles for loss while completely neutralizing Mississippi State's running game. It's been a group effort for the Crimson Tide with 300-pounders Devan Thompkins and Terance Green leading the way as chief disruptors. Edge: AlabamaSecondary Five games into the season, a full evaluation of Georgia's secondary remains challenging because of the lackluster nature of the Bulldogs' competition. Alabama leads the SEC with eight interceptions compared to four for Georgia. But the Bulldogs are allowing just 9.27 yards per completion, which is seventh nationally. 
There are different identities here. Alabama's secondary is opportunistic and apt to force big plays while also more likely to surrender them. Of course, the Crimson Tide have actually played opponents capable of generating explosive pass plays, whereas Georgia has not. They are also fairly even in terms of talent. Both secondaries landed two players on the CBS Sports preseason All-American list (Ellis Robinson IV and KJ Bolden from Georgia | Zabien Brown and Bray Hubbard from Alabama). Edge: evenCoaching Alabama's Kalen DeBoer won his first two meetings against Georgia's Kirby Smart before the Bulldogs manhandled the Crimson Tide 28-7 in last year's SEC Championship Game. That was just Smart's second win against Alabama in nine tries, but it was a sign that perhaps his staff has figured out how to handle DeBoer's style of play.
Smart owns a 2-0 edge on DeBoer in national titles and entered the season six spots ahead of DeBoer in the CBS Sports Power Four coach rankings. Considering this is their fourth meeting in three seasons, there is plenty of familiarity. Despite his poor record against Alabama, Smart is the more proven coach. Edge: GeorgiaFinal TallyCategoryGeorgiaAlabamaQB✅Skill✅OL✅Front 7✅Secondary━━Coaching✅

Everything appears to favor Dallas on Thursday night, but the Buccaneers fit the profile of a desperate winless team that has historically been primed for a breakthrough

        The Dallas Cowboys are a huge favorite going into Thursday night's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, which isn't all that surprising. After all, the Buccaneers have exactly zero wins and they have to hit the road on a short week to play in a city where they almost never win. The Cowboys are 13-2 all-time at home against the Buccaneers, which is the second-best winning percentage for any team at home against one opponent (minimum 15 games played). In those 15 games, the Buccaneers averaged just 13.2 points per game, the second-worst mark since the 1970 merger for a road team in a single city. And let's not forget that the Bucs are 1-9 in their past 10 primetime games dating back to the start of the 2023 season. Also, the Bucs will have an undrafted rookie at quarterback in Jalon Daniels, who will be making his first career start on the road. The deck certainly seems to be stacked against Tampa Bay, but there is one stat that should have the Cowboys worried. Going into this season, there had been 10 teams in NFL history that:
started 0-4 Were outscored by a combined total of 21 points or fewer in those four gamesThose 10 teams combined to go 9-1 in Week 5. The Buccaneers are now the seventh team to meet those qualifications. Yes, they're 0-4, but all four losses have come in close games that were decided by seven points or fewer. Week 1: Bengals 33-27 over Buccaneers Week 2: Browns 23-19 over BuccaneersWeek 3: Vikings 23-16 over BuccaneersWeek 4: Packers 17-14 over BuccaneersThe Bucs have been close in each game. They just haven't been able to get over the hump to pick up their first win. Overall, they've been outscored by just 20 points in those four games combined. 
Of the previous 10 teams to start 0-4 while being outscored by 21 points or less, six of them went on to win by at least a touchdown in Week 5. 1952 Steelers (Road): Pittsburgh 34-28 over Chicago Cardinals1961 Steelers (Home): Pittsburgh 20-0 over Washington1974 Lions (Home): Detroit 17-13 over San Francisco1991 Buccaneers (Road): Detroit 31-3 over Tampa Bay1998 Bears (Home): Chicago 31-27 over Detroit2000 Patriots (Road): New England 28-19 over Denver2005 Packers (Home): Green Bay 52-3 over New Orleans2011 Vikings (Home): Minnesota 34-10 over Arizona2012 Saints (Home): New Orleans 31-24 over San Diego Chargers2017 Chargers (Road): Los Angeles 27-22 over GiantsNot only are the 10 teams 9-1, but they're also 3-1 on the road, where the Bucs will be on Thursday night. 
So why is this happening? It's hard to say for sure, but when you're losing close games, that gives you confidence that you can play with anyone and if you combine that with the desperation that comes with being 0-4, it sets the stage for an upset. Of course, as you can see, the only 0-4 team in this situation that didn't win was the 1991 Buccaneers, so Tampa Bay knows first-hand that a win on Thursday night isn't a lock. As a matter of fact, it would be a total surprise if the Bucs won, but if they do pull off the upset, don't say we didn't warn you.

Three of the four League Division Series are in the books, and we're handing out fictional hardware for each

        The first two rounds of the 2026 MLB postseason are nearly complete and three of the four Championship Series teams have been decided. The Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers will again meet in the NLCS. For the ALCS, the Tampa Bay Rays await either the Chicago White Sox or Cleveland Guardians. The White Sox have a 2-1 lead in that Division Series. MLB  hands out two (really three) awards each the  postseason: World  Series  MVP and one MVP for each of the two  Championship Series. There  is  nothing to recognize the best player in  the Wild Card Series or   Division Series though, and we're here to  right that wrong. Here are our hypothetical Wild Card Series MVPs and now here three of our four Division Series MVPs. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Guardians vs. White Sox: TBA This ALDS matchup has not yet been decided. The White Sox have a 2-1 series lead and can punch their ticket to their first ALCS since 2005 as soon as Thursday night. The Guardians will look to become the first team to come back from an 0-2 deficit in the ALDS since Cleveland themselves blew a 2-0 series lead in 2017. Check back for our hypothetical ALDS MVP when this series ends. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Rays vs. Yankees: Drew Rasmussen The Rays swept the Yankees but the series wasn't really lopsided. Tampa won two one-run games and a three-run game, and they needed New York to kick the ball around like Little Leaguers in Game 2. Three of their five runs that game were unearned. The Rays hit .208/.255/.344 in the three-game sweep. Not exactly a powerhouse offensive showing, you know? 
Jonathan Aranda has strong ALDS MVP case. He went 4 for 12 in the three games and hit the solo homer that gave the Rays a 1-0 win in Game 1. This has to be Drew Rasmussen though, right? Rasmussen made Aranda's solo homer stand up by taking a no-hitter into the eighth inning. He struck out 10 and was simply sensational. "I think he's pretty special and dialed in most nights," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "As the game continues to unfold and you keep looking up there, no hits, no hits, no hits, I mean, that tells you right there. That's just a really good lineup, very elite hitting, quality at-bats, hard contact, everything.  For him to limit it that way speaks loudest about how good he was tonight." Rasmussen led all players in this series in both win probability and championship probability added, and not by a little either. He has been a Yankees Killer throughout his career (1.81 ERA in 11 starts vs. New York), and he certainly shut them down in Game 1. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
     Brewers vs. Padres: Jackson Chourio It's funny, Jackson Chourio went only 3 for 16 (.188) in the four-game NLDS, but the three hits were so impactful that he is an easy pick for NLDS MVP over William Contreras (6 for 16 with two homers) and Christian Yelich (5 for 14). Aaron Ashby's three no-hit innings of relief in the Game 4 clincher earned him some MVP consideration, too. How can it not be Chourio though? He slugged the game-tying two-run homer in Game 1, then flipped a 3-2 deficit into a 4-3 walk-off win with his two-out, two-strike, two-run single against Mason Miller in Game 2. That walk-off single completely changed the NLDS and gave Milwaukee a commanding 2-0 series lead. "I look back to my first year, my rookie year, it was a game against Seattle. I think I was the last out, punched out against (Andrés) Muñoz.  He was on the mound at that time," Chourio explained after Game 2. "At that point, everything turned for me.  I told myself I was never going to make the last out.  I'd dedicate myself to fighting and doing whatever I could for the team and not having that feeling again from that specific game." 
By championship probability added, Chourio's walk-off single is by far the biggest hit of the 2026 season to date at +6.94%. It easily clears Austin Riley's go-ahead three-run homer in Game 1 of the Wild Card Series (+3.97%). Chourio may have only hit .188 in the NLDS, but it's hard to argue any player in the series was more impactful. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Dodgers vs. Braves: Yoshinobu Yamamoto Andy Pages was a strong consideration here. He had two hits in Games 3 and 4, including what proved to be the series-winning two-run single in the seventh inning in Game 4. It was quite a redemption arc for Pages, who was so bad last postseason that he was not in the starting lineup for Games 6 and 7 of the World Series. In the end though, Yoshinobu Yamamoto was again the best player in a postseason series. He struck out 10 in seven innings of one-run ball in Game 3, which gave Los Angeles a 2-1 series lead. There is no better big-game pitcher in the game today, and Yamamoto put the Dodgers in position to return to the NLDS with his Game 3 masterpiece. 
"Wow.  What a performance," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "I think it was that fifth inning where they started to get a little bit of stress, but managed the situation, limited damage.  And to go out there and give us two more, pretty impressive ... To get through seven innings, our bullpen is in a good spot as far as Game 4.  Can't say enough about Yoshinobu." In three MLB seasons, Yamamoto owns a 2.14 ERA in 63 career postseason innings spanning 10 starts and one very memorable relief appearance. The career postseason stats don't factor into the NLDS MVP decision, but Game 3 was just more of the same from him. Yamamoto was terrific.

Five games to watch closely in a Week 6 teeming with upset potential

        Week 6 brings another round of upset opportunities, including two Big Ten matchups capable of changing the conversation well beyond the weekend and the nation's top-ranked team facing a rivalry bout with a cornered rival opponent.UCLA's trip to Oregon is a narrative-setter. The Bruins have a chance to turn growing respect into something more substantial with a win, while the Ducks will turn to Dylan Raiola at quarterback after Dante Moore was ruled out with a concussion.Matt Rhule has a chance for a signature win at Nebraska against reigning national champion Indiana. The Huskers have spent years waiting for a breakthrough on this stage, but have failed to deliver after every opportunity.Which favorites should be nervous this week? Here are the games with enough warning signs to demand attention in Week 6.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 1 TexasOpponent: vs. Oklahoma (+7.5)The Sooners could turn the tide on a disappointing start to the season with a win over the hated Longhorns in the Cotton Bowl. For that to happen, Oklahoma needs the best out of John Mateer at quarterback, a player who has underachieved all season so far. Brent Venables said this week his staff evaluated its options under center during the open date ahead of Texas, but stopped short of providing any additional details. Texas' defense has been rolling since the fourth quarter against Ohio State, including a dominant 10-sack performance in the team's win at Tennessee. After losing four straight to Oklahoma, the Longhorns won three of the last four in the series by an average of 32.3 points per game.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 11 OregonOpponent: vs. UCLA (+11.5)If anyone could conceal a hot mic in UCLA's locker room before this one, we would appreciate it. Bob Chesney's pre-game speech should go something like this: "We're unbeaten, a double-digit underdog, and nobody believes in us." That essentially covers the bases in the Big Ten's game of the weekend at Autzen Stadium. Both squads had ample time to prepare after the open date. UCLA leads the Big Ten in rushing, and the Ducks are explosive on offense. Fireworks? They're coming. UCLA leads the all-time series with Oregon, 38-35, but the Ducks have won five straight in the series dating back to the 2018 season and 11 of their last 12 meetings overall.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 20 IowaOpponent: at Washington (-3.5)Another example of a ranked team going on the road as an underdog that usually cashes for the home team. We saw this a few weeks ago when Florida was favored against unbeaten, then-No. 4 Ole Miss before blowing out the Rebels. 
Husky Stadium on a Friday night will be a raucous environment, and Washington badly needs a victory after narrow Big Ten losses to Minnesota and USC. The Hawkeyes must limit Demond Williams. Priority No. 1 last week was corralling Jeremiah Smith, and it didn't happen during a 31-14 loss to Ohio State. Letting another one of the opponent's best players cook is not a winning recipe for Kirk Ferentz's team.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 7 IndianaOpponent: at Nebraska (+7.5)Nebraska has lost 31 consecutive games against top-25 teams dating back to the 2016 season, including all nine in Matt Rhule's tenure as coach. However, there's reason for optimism entering Saturday's bout with Indiana, which carries a 21-game winning streak into the ring. The defending national champions don't look as invincible as they once did if the Huskers can man up at the line of scrimmage.
Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr. have already combined for more than 1,000 yards rushing this fall with nine touchdowns, but Nebraska prides itself on stopping the run. The Hoosiers also haven't yet faced a quarterback as dynamic as Anthony Colandrea, who has been a home-run replacement for Dylan Raiola. Indiana has already failed to cover against one Big Ten opponent this season, and that came at home. If there was ever a spot for Nebraska's coming-out party and leap into the top 25, this is it.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 14 MissouriOpponent: vs. Texas A&M (+3.5)This is a classic trap spot for the Tigers, coming off the blowout win over previously unbeaten Florida. The Tigers' mammoth win was impressive, but only laying 3.5 points against a desperate Texas A&M team shows that oddsmakers understand this one comes with a warning.The Aggies are trying to keep their season from sinking, and urgency can make an inconsistent team dangerous. Coach Mike Elko remains a believer in Marcel Reed, whose flashes suggest there's more available than Texas A&M has shown during an uneven campaign. 
If Reed protects the football and makes Missouri defend his legs, this could get uncomfortable quickly. Eli Drinkwitz said last week his team's only priority is blocking out the noise and focusing on getting better week to week. Another barometer matchup comes Saturday.

        Week 6 of the college football season brings the beginning of mid-week action, and that includes the CBS Sports Network slate where there will be six games across four days on the network. That starts Wednesday night at 7 p.m. ET when Jacksonville State heads to Kennesaw State for a rematch of last year's Conference USA title game that the Gamecocks won. On Thursday, Missouri State will travel to Western Kentucky at 7 p.m. for another CUSA conference tilt between a pair of one-win teams desperate to keep their dreams of a bowl game alive. title: How Ashley Sanchez found joy again, thrived in new position and got back in USWNT mix - CBS Sports
description: When you have a career year and match a single-season goal-scoring record of 20 goals in NWSL, the spotlight brightens quickly. Your ski
body:
When you have a career year and match a single-season goal-scoring record of 20 goals in NWSL, the spotlight brightens quickly. Your skills end up in more social media clips, you earn more league recognition, and you gain overall honors. You also get way more media requests. North Carolina Courage forward Ashley Sanchez is having a personal-best season. Drafted in 2020, she's playing a new position as a winger and has become the first American player to score 20 goals in the NWSL regular season. While she still has a handful of games to set an even more impressive record, she found time for an interview with CBS Sports after a club training session while on her way home with a teammate in the car."I'm here with Ryan [Williams] too in the car, so don't say anything bad about her," she joked. For Sanchez, navigating the brighter spotlight means blocking most of it out altogether. She's on the verge of breaking a league goal-scoring record, recently engaged, and now back in national team camps for the first time since January 2025.
"I mean, definitely, [more attention] is a little bit different, but I think I just try not to care too much about outside noise or opinions, and just try to, like, control myself and the product that I have on the field. I think also part of it is, I feel like I have done a lot more than maybe I thought I was gonna do. So, now it's just all this other stuff is just kind of extra," she explained about the increased attention."I feel like I just keep setting the bar for myself, but a lot of that is definitely not listening to other people and their opinions and just not getting too high about all this extra stuff. We still have so many games left and so much more to do. So yeah, I guess I don't want to say I don't care, but I kind of guess I just don't care too much."Finding the joy in soccer once againSanchez's previous career highs were back-to-back five-goal seasons -- her final year with the Washington Spirit in 2023, and her first season with North Carolina after being traded there in 2024. Her efforts in earlier seasons with the Spirit earned her more national team call-ups, where she was considered among the "next gen" core of players, and she even made the 2023 World Cup roster with the U.S. national team, though Sanchez was one of three players who didn't get to play a single minute in the tournament. 
The disappointment took some of the joy out of the sport for her, and with a new head coach and a smaller roster for the Olympics, she ultimately missed the gold medal run at the 2024 Summer Olympics. Then 2025 presented a new career low: two goals over 23 appearances and a season where staff and players couldn't find the chemistry with each other. She shifted her personal goals ahead of her 2026 club season to just find the joy again, have fun, and be a good teammate."The last couple years, I haven't had as much fun playing, and I felt like this year it definitely just took a turn, and I felt like I was really enjoying myself on and off the field, and just cherishing every moment. Going into a more of a leadership role. I mean, we have so many young players on there on my team, and I just feel like wanting to help them in any way that I can and be a good example of a leader and just a veteran on the team," Sanchez said.The small, personal changes helped make her strides in 2026 all the more obvious. The 20 goals are no fluke. They're a combination of internal work and the product of a positional switch with deliberate individual planning for the player.
North Carolina Courage head coach Mak Lind is in year one with the club. He joined from BK Hacken, where he turned the team into annual UEFA Women's Champions League participants, and he was tasked with defining a style of play and getting the team back to sustainable success."Yeah, I mean, before I even signed my contract with the Courage, you could see a player in Ashley Sanchez being an incredible player with her attributes. I think this season she has found couple of keys in her game, which makes her so dangerous offensively. It is not a coincidence that she keeps scoring goals that are very important for us. She has to thank herself because she's an incredible player with attributes. We just helped her with a couple of keys and how to unlock that potential. That potential has already been there before, so I'm very happy for her. I'm proud of her," said Lind.Positional switch that unlocked potentialThere's a leap of faith and a layer of trust that's needed when approaching a switch in position. Part of Lind's eagerness to take the head coaching role with the Courage was the chance to coach in NWSL and work with a player like Sanchez. It was an immediate no-brainer for the coach to chat with his future player about his longer-term vision for her. His first priority was getting Sanchez into a role where she would thrive. 
"That was, for me, very clear. The first week already, when I was here. We talked about her position, and for me, Ashley Sanchez is a winger, and especially on the left-hand side, she shows again how good she can be. At the same time, she is so skilled that I think she can play in different positions," said Lind."But I think if you want to get the most out of Ashley Sanchez, you play her in a wing position where she has the freedom of playing wide, she has the freedom of inverting in pocket positioning, and be dangerous there. So, I'm very happy for her, and her performances in the season have been very consistent and helped us win games and score many goals," he said.For Sanchez, it was a fairly easy conversation to have with Lind considering her light-hearted, no-pressure approach to this season. 
"Going into a new position this year, the goals that I had for myself were definitely more attacking-minded than maybe I did in the past. Just more like end-product assists and goals, and I didn't really have a number, but I definitely surpassed what I thought that number would be for sure," Sanchez said on her positional switch."Definitely feels pretty natural. As soon as preseason started, I pretty much went into that role, but I definitely think it's good for the qualities that I have as a player, and I think it just puts me in really good positions and being closer to goal and still being able to play make. Going into more one-on-one situations, which I definitely think is a strength of mine, but it's been really fun. I feel like I still have a lot more to learn, but definitely happy with the position I've been playing this year," she said.The winger also credits her life off the pitch for keeping her grounded. Whether leaning on her faith, support from her fiancé Thomas Williamson, or their new dog Benny, they're all things that have aligned for Sanchez and helped with her success on the pitch this year.
"Having a good support system and home life makes it a lot easier to just have this job. But I also think a lot of it just comes with maybe me having just peace outside of soccer, and something else like an outlet. So I'm not as taken over by soccer and just all-consuming," she explained."It's nice to have the support, and my fiancé played soccer, so he understands, and it's nice being able to go over games, and someone who just understands what I'm doing and giving me pointers and stuff, but I definitely feel like I'm just really happy off the field, which also helps translate on the field."It's also the leadership aspect that's changed for Sanchez. Once considered among the next wave of stars for the league, with future international potential, and drafted in 2020 alongside Sophia Wilson and in close proximity to Trinity Rodman (2021), and Naomi Girma (2022), Sanchez is now in her seventh year as an NWSL pro. 
While she's always open to being coached up, she's no longer the 20-year-old who left college early to play in the big leagues. Her maturity is a noticeable change for her and her teammates, and they're celebrating her success."It's been really, really fun to see. Obviously, we're really close friends, so I'm just really happy for Ash. I'm not surprised by it, just based off of what we get to see every day in training," said Williams."She works so hard, she puts in the work, she really pays her dues in a way where she does all these things in training, and everybody else gets to see like a really small portion of that in games. So it's just really nice to see that she's getting rewarded in games with so many goals and assists and breaking records and all these things. So we're really happy for her, and yeah, I'm not surprised by it."
Career year leads back to USWNT campsWith her club form finally taking off, it revived a familiar conversation about her inclusion around the national team. While she didn't play in the 2023 World Cup, senior caps also became scarcer between coaches, with her last cap in October 2024 -- after Hayes and the team won Olympic gold and she has mostly been outside of the larger pool of players ever since. Sanchez's last senior-level call-up under Emma Hayes was in January 2025. Sanchez's run of goal scoring started early this year; by June she had seven goals, but things like timing, schedules, and opportunities rarely align, and with one fewer international window this year due to the 2026 FIFA men's World Cup, there was a question whether or not a call-up would pan out for Sanchez.Especially in the larger ecosystem that Hayes and her staff are developing for the program with U.S. Soccer. Previously, Hayes has said in media settings that she wants players to make decisions hard for her, and that for some players, it can take, on average, roughly six camps to truly get acclimated to the environment. But even for Hayes, what Sanchez is doing for club cannot be ignored, and while there are some overage players in the U23 camps, that's not where she wants to see Sanchez performing for now.
"We always think, of course, we want to get closer to the team that's going to play for us in qualifiers -- and it might not be those that are coming into their first ever cap with us, but it's a great moment to bring them in and see how well they have learned from the U23s," Hayes told CBS Sports."I think you know me well enough to know now, there's going to be minimal changes between game one and game two [against Spain], so there can be players that have not played, but they get the chance to. We get the chance to see how they can cope without the pressure of that. Our job is qualifying, but at the same time, if you want to win [future tournaments], there might be a player that enters into that,"  she said.The USWNT manager is full steam ahead on preparing for World Cup qualifiers in November, with an eye on the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup, but she's also thinking longer term. Developing players, utilizing the revamped U23 program as an extension of the player pool, so that longer-term planning for future competitions seems more natural. In Sanchez's case, with one less international window, the timing is now, even if Spain are clearly the USWNT's biggest test of the year. If the June window wasn't in the plans for a then seven-goals-scored Sanchez, the only real chance is now. Perhaps that's a little unfair, but with a league-record amount of goals, and only one window before qualifiers, and just three next year before the 2027 World Cup, time is running out for the coaching staff to see what Sanchez can bring to the squad, whether or not there are six camp windows available for a player to get re-acclimated."You have to think of it like that. It's too long [in between windows] if we say, 'Oh, we've already made it, didn't think Ashley Sanchez was part of our plan, stick with the group that we've been building towards it.' When's the next moment she's going to get it? November? No, we wouldn't do it then because we're going to qualify. January is pre-season. What are we going to see? Are we going to do it in February? She's still in pre-season. Is she going to [play] up? Okay, so we wait till April?" Hayes explained."So yes, changes have to happen sometimes. It's not because we're going to always experiment with the team and the lineup, but sometimes it's to give someone a look to say, 'do we actually think player X is further ahead than the player who might have gone to U23?' Yes or no? Let's have a look now, because I know what Jaedyn Shaw looks like, I know what Ally Sentnor looks like, for example."While Hayes isn't outright revealing her starters for the games already, she's told reporters that no first-time camp players will start against Spain, though they should be prepared for minutes if their name is called. Sanchez fits into a unique scenario in that it's been nearly two years since her last appearance in a senior jersey, and now her next one could come against the world's No. 1-ranked team. While Sanchez is making the decisions harder for coaches and defenders on the pitch, the road she's traveled to return to the top of her game hasn't been easy. A welcome back to national team camps should be viewed as more than well-earned. For Sanchez, she's keeping things level and not letting other things define success after working through lows to get back to joy on the pitch."I think there's like a lot of things. I feel like there's a lot of people that go through, maybe what I've kind of been through, where I'm just kind of in a little bit of -- like not a slump, but you know, tough things are happening," said Sanchez."I think like just having the mindset of taking control of what I can and just like making sure I'm not giving up or throwing in the towel. I think a lot of times when hard things happen, we can kind of become a victim, and I really tried to just push through, and I felt like I knew that I was going to get rewarded at the end of the day, and I just kept my faith in that, and at the end of the day, that's all you can do."

body:
As the 2026 Major League Baseball season continues to unfold, something vitally important to the future of the sport quietly hums in the background: the ongoing negotiations over a new collective bargaining agreement. The collective bargaining agreement, or CBA  (or Basic Agreement, as it's known in a formal sense), is the negotiated accord between players and clubs -- i.e., the team owners and commissioner Rob Manfred, who represents their interests -- that governs the working relationship between the two parties, typically for a period of five years. It covers things as mundane as players' meal allowances and travel protocols and as vital as minimum salaries, the structure of free agency, revenue-sharing specifics, and roster sizes. Every CBA can be distilled down to a fight over money, or, more specifically, how the league's revenues will be divided between players and team owners. The first CBA covered the 1968 and 1969 seasons and was the first in professional sports history. That was the handiwork of Marvin Miller, the pioneering head of the Players Association (i.e., the players union) and belated Hall of Famer. It was Miller's organizing skills, foresight, and training as a union economist that allowed him to make the Players Association a viable and effective labor organization. Every CBA negotiation from 1972 through 1994-95 resulted in some form and scale of labor stoppage, whether a players' strike or an owner-implemented lockout. After the cancellation of the 1994 World Series because of the worst labor stoppage in the sport's history, a long run of peace followed. That peace lasted until the prior CBA negotiations, which resulted in a 99-day lockout forced by team owners and delayed the start of the 2022 season. 
        
            
                MLB's new CBA proposal would restrict free-agency contracts, raise minimum wage, but only with a salary cap
                
                    Dayn Perry                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The current CBA negotiations have been underway for some time, and not surprisingly, the two sides remain far apart on several key issues. The biggest fight will be over the owners' renewed desire to implement a salary cap, which the union continues to view as a non-starter. The push for a cap has less to do with the notions of competitive balance and more to do with the ownership's internal belief that being the only non-salary-capped league among the major North American sports is harming franchise values. The cap, though, is but one of many pressing issues on which players and owners must find congruity.
Moving forward, the process will be uncertain and rife with posturing and pointed public comments from both sides. The hope, though, is that a new CBA will be agreed to before the middle of March 2027, at which point there's a high risk of having the 2027 season delayed or even abbreviated. To keep you informed of the twists and turns along the way to a new CBA, we've provided a detailed timeline of negotiations. That timeline will illuminate the important and finer points of the talks and, along the way, explain the implications of the various proposals coming from each side. The hope, of course, is that all of it culminates in a timely agreement that permits a fully intact and on-time 2027 season. Now let's begin. Oct. 8, 2026: MLB proposes 154-game season, postseason changesIn its latest proposal, MLB proposed reducing the regular season from 162 games to 154 games, and adding a standard off day to every week. The league also proposed extending the Division Series from a best-of-five to a best-of-seven, and allowing higher seeded teams to select their opponents in the Wild Card Series and Division Series. As with every MLB proposal to date, the 154-game schedule and changes to the postseason format are contingent on the MLBPA accepting a salary car/floor system.
Sept. 28, 2026: A 60-game mark could be crucial in 2027If labor strife lops off 60 or more games from the 2027 MLB season, then the consequences could be significant. The Athletic recently reported that if the forthcoming lockout extends into late May or so and costs at least 60 games, then most of the league's national broadcast and streaming contracts would be extended for another year, through 2029. That's significant because commissioner Rob Manfred hopes to bundle and centralize team streaming rights and share those revenues equally, and the current timeline would theoretically allow that to happen at the same time the national contracts are up for renegotiation. Tacking on another year to those national contracts would push back the significant windfall that owners and the league are expecting from that new media rights structure. As such, this is a heavy incentive, at least on the league side, to not let any labor stoppage drag into June. Sept. 2, 2026: Anonymous poll of players shows unity -- but not unanimity -- against capA poll of current MLB players across the full spectrum of salaries and service time conducted by ESPN showed strong resistance to the payroll cap and floor being demanded by ownership and league and being put forth as a precondition to every proposed change from that side. An excerpt: How open are you to a salary cap?NL starting pitcher entering arbitration: Not open.NL infielder making eight figures annually: Zero. No chance.NL infielder on two-year contract: Zero. Absolute zero.NL pre-arbitration journeyman: From what I've been told, I don't think it's good for the game. I just don't know if I know all the pros and cons of it. But, from everything we've been told, it doesn't sound like it's a good thing.NL reliever on multiyear contract: With the right criteria, I'd be open to it.AL starting pitcher in arbitration: I don't want it. In '94, they canceled the World Series, so if those guys can miss over half a year and miss the World Series, I think we're fully prepared to hold out for sure.AL catcher entering arbitration: I need more information, but perhaps I would listen on it.That's mostly strong sentiment that aligns with the MLBPA position on the cap, but it's not ironclad. MLB in negotiations and its public statements is seeking to tap into any existing divide between, broadly speaking, lower-salaried players with not much service time and more tenured veterans in their higher-earning years. There is a bit of a schism there, but it would take a substantial one to shift, in any exploitable way, the union's long-standing opposition to a cap-and-floor system. The ESPN piece covers an array of CBA topics. With the two questions related to the proposed cap, the responses can be broken down as 16 in mostly firm opposition to a cap and five not necessarily in favor but open to further discussions and reflection. Aug. 27, 2026: MLB proposes changes to roster rules, free agencyMLB proposed a series of changes to current roster rules that, in a statement, the league says are aimed at "creating more stability in rosters, getting the best players to the  Major Leagues more quickly, and accelerating the pace of the offseason." Among the rule changes included in MLB's proposal are:Weekly rosters that are set each Monday. Only roster changes necessitated by injury, bereavement, paternity leave, trades, and waivers would be allowed after weekly rosters are set.Teams would be allowed to carry 14 pitchers on their 26-man roster. The current limit is 13.The 10-day (position players) and 15-day (pitchers) injured lists would be reduced to one week and two weeks, respectively. The 60-day injured list would be replaced with a 12-week injured list.Yearly optional assignments to the minors would be reduced from five to four. Currently, players can be called up and sent down only five times per season. After that, waivers are required.Move Rule 5 Draft eligibility up one year and allow players selected in the Rule 5 Draft to go to the minors. Currently, players selected in the Rule 5 Draft must remain on the MLB roster all season.Two separate "Quiet Periods" at the start and end of the offseason that limit free agent signings between the first day of the Winter Meetings and Dec. 21. Trades would still be allowed throughout the entire offseason. In a statement, MLBPA interim head Bruce Meyer said an "artificial free agency window ... would reduce player leverage and create a game of musical chairs pitting player vs. player."All the proposed roster rule changes are contingent on the MLB Players Association agreeing to a salary cap-and-floor system.July 21, 2026: MLBPA proposes changes to draftDuring a negotiating session with the league, the players' union puts forth its own proposed changes to the MLB Draft -- changes that are, in essence, a rejoinder to the drastic overhaul earlier put forward by MLB. Among the changes the MLBPA proposes are: Continued draft eligibility for high school and junior college players and expanded eligibility in the college ranks to include sophomores;Preserving the current 20-round draft format;An increase in the amount of money allotted toward draft signing bonuses;Continuing to award additional competitive balance draft picks to small-market and lower-revenue clubs;Rejecting proposed hard slot bonuses and continuing to allow draftees to negotiate their bonuses;Allowing lower revenue clubs to increase their signing bonus pool for the draft and implementing automatic pool increases for lower-revenue teams that qualify for postseason play;A reduction to the penalties levied against teams that exceed their draft bonus pool;Allowing the trading of draft picks among teams, with some as yet unnamed restrictions;Moving the draft back to June.Additionally, the union proposes increasing the money payable to draftees under the incentive bonus plan and eliminating, according to the MLBPA, "the current practice of clubs deducting certain bonuses from players' continuing education benefits."The timing of the draft has actually been a concern for front offices for years, since it was shifted later in the calendar to coincide with the All-Star break in 2021. Holding the draft in July crams both that and the trade deadline into just a few weeks and making it more difficult to allocate resources.July 14, 2026: The sparring continuesCommissioner Rob Manfred and interim union head Bruce Meyer each hold press conferences on the day of the All-Star Game in Philadelphia. "I think that I have an ownership group that is more united than any group in my entire time of baseball," Manfred says, referring at least obliquely to the league's push for a salary cap. "They are a group that believes in what I am arguing for.""The supposed stewards of the game have spent an inordinate amount of time trying to convince those same fans that they don't have hope or they shouldn't have hope or that the product that they're paying to consume in record numbers is somehow broken," Meyer says of MLB's efforts to highlight perceived competitive-balance issues in the face of increasing attendance and television ratings. "I think it's perverse."
July 1, 2026: Temporary roster size expansionThe MLBPA puts forth multiple proposals, many of them dealing with procedural matters for purposes of player health, safety, and wellness. They include: Expanding MLB active rosters from 26 to 28 (14 pitcher maximum) for the first 15 days of the regular season. Allowing for placement of players on the 60-day injured list as early as the November tender deadline.Reducing the number of permissible in-season optional assignments per player from five to three.Accelerating eligibility for the Rule 5 Draft and ensuring a Rule 5 Draft will be held in 2026 and each year of the next CBA.Providing MLB service time and salary protections to pitchers who are optioned to the minors over the All-Star break and or immediately after a game where they met certain performance thresholds.Enabling all players to access club-collected non-proprietary performance data and video.The union's latest proposal is a reminder of the breadth of CBA discussions. Most issues are not the big-ticket items like a salary cap or lack thereof or revenue sharing structure but instead are somewhat esoteric matters that strike most fans as mundane. To players and teams, though, they're important considerations and in some instances may even provide a foundation of common ground moving forward. June 25, 2026: Limited free-agency contractsMore face-to-face negotiations take place, and MLB proposes more changes to the free-agency system, among other asks. MLB's latest proposal includes the following, all of which depend upon the union's acceptance of a payroll cap:
A maximum contract length of five years for players who switch teams and a maximum of 15% of the cap with 5% increases every year of the contract;A maximum contract length of six years -- and a max of 16% of the cap -- for players who remain with their original team under a new "Cornerstone Player" provision;Based on the league's proposed cap figure for 2027, the maximum contract for a player switching teams is $202 million over five years and $265 million over six years for a player remaining with the same team;An increase in the minimum salary from $780,000 to $1 million for players with at least two years of MLB service time;An increase in the minimum salary to $900,000 for players with less than two years of MLB service time with the opportunity for a $100,000 bonus from the pre-arbitration bonus pool (already established);The elimination of deferred contracts;Acceptance of the union's proposal to allow free agency after five years of MLB service time instead of six for players age 30 or older;Acceptance of the union's proposal to do away with the qualifying offer system for free agents.MLB in a prior proposal called for a cap on team payrolls of $245.3 million starting in 2027 and a payroll floor of $171.2 million. The league issues a statement that reads in full: "The biggest issue baseball fans want solved to strengthen the game is fixing the payroll disparity that leaves too many fans without hope of their team competing for a World Series title. Every other major U.S. sport has tackled this problem, and every year more small market teams in those leagues have a chance to win. The salary cap and floor proposal levels the playing field, allowing us greater flexibility to address longstanding player priorities while sharing baseball revenue with the players 50/50."Today, in addition to proposing the largest ever increase in the minimum salary, earned by over half of MLB players, we accepted two landmark changes to free agency that have been in place for 50 years. We agreed to both the MLBPA's proposal to provide earlier access to free agency, and their proposal to eliminate the qualifying offer system, a provision players view as a drag on free agency. We also proposed to eliminate deferred compensation and to create a new 'Cornerstone Player' provision similar to the NBA's 'Bird Rights' to give every team a fair shot at retaining their fans' favorite star players."We will continue working with the MLBPA during the bargaining process to improve the game for teams, players and fans."The MLBPA responds: "After making a series of proposals to reduce player compensation by billions of dollars, eliminate fundamental rights with a salary cap, and destroy the amateur entry process, Major League Baseball and team owners are now attempting to distract from the true impact their plan would have on baseball. These misleading offers are designed to look like 'improvements' but are of little or no value, given they are expressly conditioned on agreement to the league's cap system which eliminates the free market, and ensures gains for one player only come at the expense of another. "The league also introduced a litany of additional restrictions on player rights — limiting salaries, contract length, performance, award, and signing bonuses. While MLB claims to be acting in the interest of fans, their proposals thus far are entirely consistent with owners' long-held goals: suppressing player salaries and maximizing club profits. "Owners' attempts to pit players against players are nothing new, but they've failed in the past and will fail again now, because PA members remain unified. We are committed to achieving a fair deal that protects the rights of all players, promotes competition, and leaves our game better for future generations."Lacking from the league's latest proposal, at least on the public-facing side, is any revisiting of the recent changes to the draft and any mention of prior proposed changes to the league's revenue-sharing system. 
During these same face-to-face sessions, the MLBPA proposes a ban on prop bets placed on individual players, ESPN reports. The idea is to preempt harrassment of players by gamblers. The proposed ban would extend to bets placed on individual player performance prior to and during any MLB game. The MLBPA also requested that players be permitted to engage in paid endorsements and sponsorships with sportsbooks and prediction markets. June 18, 2026: MLB proposes sweeping draft changesMLB and the MLBPA meet for face-to-face negotiations, and owners propose sweeping changes to the draft and also push for an international draft. As for the MLB Draft, formally known as the First-Year Player Draft, MLB pushes for the following changes:A reduction from 20 rounds to 12 rounds;A $200 million hard bonus system in which players are paid according to their draft position with no room to negotiate (teams have not spent $200 million or less in the draft since 2010);High school players would no longer be eligible for the domestic amateur draft, and college players would be draft-eligible at age 20."Over the last several years, college baseball has undergone a remarkable transformation," MLB says in a statement. "Expanded scholarships, NIL opportunities, revenue sharing and significant investments in facilities and player development have made college baseball an increasingly important pathway that is producing major league-ready talent at an accelerated rate. Today's top programs provide players with resources, competition and national exposure that were unimaginable a decade ago. Our proposal is designed to build on that momentum to benefit the game at the college, minor-league and major-league levels. By creating a draft system centered around college-aged players and making most college players eligible one year earlier, more players will benefit from both a college education and an elite development environment while reaching professional baseball -- and ultimately the major leagues -- more quickly. We believe these changes will strengthen college baseball and deepen fans' connection to the next generation of major league stars. We look forward to working with the MLBPA throughout the bargaining process to modernize the domestic amateur system in a way that benefits players, clubs, and fans." 
As for the international draft, MLB proposed making players outside of the U.S., Puerto Rico, and Canada (who are already included in the standard draft) subject to a similar system. The international draft would, as with the proposed changes to the MLB Draft, come with a $200 million bonus cap. At present, international amateurs may sign with any team under the international free agent system, although teams do have hard budget caps each year.The MLBPA also issues a statement in response to MLB's proposals:Today, MLB made another set of proposals that are flat out bad for baseball, ones that would cripple the next generation of players and damage the future of our game. They would, among other things:Eliminate over a billion dollars in player compensation from the international and domestic system over the next five years, with a $400 million reduction from 2026 to 2027 alone.Destroy fundamental player rights and remove talent from our sport by barring high school and junior college players (anyone under age 20) from the domestic draft.Abolish an entire year of international signings by delaying the first draft until at least September of 2027 (and as late as March of 2028), denying young international players the ability to start their professional careers.Players remain committed to bargaining in good faith and leaving baseball better than they found it -- the league's proposals fall woefully short.June 5, 2026: Trump supports a capU.S. President Donald J. Trump publicly supports MLB's efforts to implement a salary cap. "If you don't have a salary cap, you don't have a sport, because they can't help themselves," Trump says. "Football has a salary cap. They should have done it a long time ago."It's shocking, frankly, that they didn't put a cap on many years ago," he said, possibly referencing the 1994-95 strike. "They had a chance to do a cap, but they blew it."June 3, 2026: Manfred talks luxury taxSpeaking to reporters following the owners' quarterly meetings, Manfred addresses the luxury-tax system he and the owners seek to replace with a cap. "We have tried mightily over several rounds of bargaining to use a competitive balance (luxury) tax to address competitive concerns," Manfred says. "And sometimes you've got to admit you failed."We made a proposal on one set of topics. At the outset of negotiations, I went and said myself, 'We're open to whatever ideas people have, but we need a realistic framework that addresses the fans' concerns about competitive balance.' You just can't ignore that financial penalties have not gotten it done for us."June 1, 2026: MLBPA says cap is 'institutionalized collusion'In a call with reporters, MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer addresses the owners' proposals. "Using MLB's definition of revenue and player share as set forth in their proposal and their presentation to us, player share under their proposal would go down," Meyer says. "Player share for this season, 2026, is projected to be well over 50 percent, using, again MLB's definitions of revenues and what counts against player share."Had MLB's proposal been in place in 2026, players, we estimate, would lose over half a billion dollars."
Meyer also refers to a salary cap as "a form of institutionalized collusion.""Our salary cap-and-floor proposal addresses our fans' concerns by leveling the playing field while sharing baseball revenue with the players 50-50 like the other leagues," MLB spokesperson Glen Caplin responded on behalf of the league. "Under our proposal, major-league players will receive more compensation in year one of the system than in 2026. We are ready to listen if the MLBPA wants to counter our proposal at the bargaining table."May 28, 2026: MLB's first proposalsMLB and the owners publicly announce their first formal CBA proposal. Chiefly, they propose: 
A salary cap, including benefits expenses, of $245.3 million for 2027;A salary floor, also including benefits expenses, of $171.2 million for 2027;A 50-50 revenue split between clubs and players;The centralization and equal sharing of all local revenues.Using competitive balance tax (CBT), or luxury tax, payrolls as a guide, since they include benefits expenses, nine teams at present would be above the proposed cap line, while 12 teams would be below the floor. However, as Craig Goldstein points out, the amount needed to get all these teams below or above the relevant payroll thresholds amounts to an $18.7 million loss in aggregate player salary overall. Another sticking point will be how league revenues are defined. Owners no doubt seek to carve out things like real estate developments surrounding ballparks and ownership stakes in regional sports. As well, MLB's working definition of league revenues includes many expense deductions. On another level, the fact that Manfred is able to persuade large-market, high-revenue clubs to agree to equal sharing of all local revenues is a notable development. However, such a concession by those large-market clubs may be contingent upon the implementation of a cap. Another sticking point is that the league proposes an escrow system, as is used in the NBA and the NHL. This would mean a percentage of player salaries is withheld. If revenues fall short of projections, some of that money in escrow goes back to the league. If revenues are higher than projected, that excess is shared with the players. The MLBPA opposes the escrow system on the grounds that it undermines the notion of guaranteed player salaries. May 27, 2026: MLBPA's first proposalsThe MLBPA makes an opening suite of proposals to the league, including:
A "competitive integrity tax" levied against teams that don't spend a minimum amount on player payroll.An increase of the minimum salary from $780,000 to $1.5 million.An increase of the bottom Competitive Balance Tax (more commonly known as the luxury tax) threshold from $244 million to $300 million.Increased sharing of local-broadcast revenues among teams but less sharing of stadium game-day revenues (the latter to incentivize on-field success).Tens of millions in extra revenue sharing to go to low-revenue teams that make the postseason or have a winning record.Free agency after five or more years, rather than six, for players who are at least 30 years of age at the time.Expanded draft lottery. Penalties for teams that neglect to spend revenue-sharing payments on team payroll.Draft picks and other incentives for low-revenue clubs active in free agency. Elimination of the qualifying offer for outgoing free agents.Increased compensation for lower-revenue teams losing players to free agency."Today, the MLBPA (Major League Baseball Players Association) presented a comprehensive set of economic proposals designed to advance the rights and benefits of players at all levels," Meyer says in a statement released by the union. "Our goal is to preserve and improve baseball's market system, rewarding competition on and off the field. Additionally, the players' proposals provide increased revenue sharing initially guaranteeing every small market club a minimum of $240m in revenue every season. This enhanced revenue sharing includes added protections to ensure clubs prioritize winning over profiteering. Ultimately, our proposals are designed to build upon the incredible momentum and popularity of our sport world-wide.""We appreciate the union making a set of proposals and we look forward to continuing the bargaining process and working towards solving the competitive balance problem our fans are telling us needs to be addressed," Caplin says in a statement. "We understand their proposals are designed to benefit players. Unfortunately, they do not address and in fact exacerbate the competitive balance problem our fans are telling us we must address. The MLBPA's proposal would reduce the amount transferred to lower-revenue Clubs, weaken the Competitive Balance Tax, and lead to even more payroll disparity than exists today. For example, under the Union's proposal, the Dodgers would pay less in luxury tax payments, giving them an additional $70 million to spend on payroll."May 12, 2026: Negotiations beginNegotiations on a new CBA formally begin between teams and players. Among the key issues to be discussed will be the league's desire for a salary cap, drastic changes to the revenue sharing system, league expansion, possible further playoff expansion, and an international draft.Dec. 1, 2026The 2022-26 Basic Agreement is set to expire at 11:59 p.m. ET, at which point owners are expected to lock out the players in the absence of a new agreement.
